docs.contenu:
🎯 Objectives
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
- Use the past simple for finished actions with a definite time.
- Use the present perfect for actions linked to the present.
- Form the present perfect with have/has + past participle.
- Choose correctly between the two tenses.

🔍 Warm-up
Compare: "I visited London in 2019." and "I have visited London." The first tells us WHEN (2019, finished). The second says the experience is true up to now, without saying when. This difference is the heart of the lesson.

I. The past simple (review)
📘 Rule (uses)
The past simple describes an action that started and finished at a DEFINITE time in the past.
📏 Form
- Regular verbs: base + -ed. play → played.
- Irregular verbs: special forms. go → went, see → saw, do → did.
- Negative: didn't + base verb.
- Question: Did + subject + base verb?
📏 Time markers
yesterday, last week, two days ago, in 2019, when I was young.
✏️ Worked examples
- We travelled to Italy last summer.
- She didn't finish her homework.
- Did you see the match yesterday?

II. The present perfect: form
📘 Rule
The present perfect connects the PAST and the PRESENT.
📏 Form
subject + have / has + past participle
- I / You / We / They + have (I've) + past participle.
- He / She / It + has (he's) + past participle.
📏 The past participle
- Regular verbs: same as past simple, base + -ed. work → worked.
- Irregular verbs: third form (learn by heart). go → gone, see → seen, do → done, eat → eaten, write → written, be → been.
📏 Negative and questions
- Negative: haven't / hasn't + past participle. I haven't seen it.
- Question: Have / Has + subject + past participle? Have you finished?

✏️ Worked examples
- I have finished my project.
- She has never eaten sushi.
- Have you ever visited Rome?

III. Uses of the present perfect
📘 Rule (uses)
1. Life experiences (no definite time): I have visited many countries.
2. Actions that started in the past and continue now (with for / since): She has lived here for ten years.
3. Recent actions with a present result: I have lost my keys (so I can't get in now).
4. Actions in an unfinished time period (today, this week): I have studied a lot this week.

📏 Key words with the present perfect
- ever, never: Have you ever been abroad? I have never flown.
- already, yet: I have already eaten. Have you finished yet? I haven't finished yet.
- just: I have just arrived.
- for + period: for two years, for a long time.
- since + starting point: since 2020, since Monday.

👀 Note (for and since)
- for + a length of time: for three days, for five years.
- since + a point in time: since Monday, since 2018, since I was a child.

IV. Past simple or present perfect?
📘 Rule (the core choice)
- Use the PAST SIMPLE when the time is finished or stated: yesterday, last year, in 2019, at 8 o'clock.
- Use the PRESENT PERFECT when the time is unstated, unfinished, or the action connects to now: ever, never, already, yet, just, for, since, this week.

📏 Compare
- I saw that film last night. (definite past time → past simple)
- I have seen that film. (experience, no time → present perfect)
- She lived in Paris for two years. (she doesn't live there now → past simple)
- She has lived in Paris for two years. (she still lives there → present perfect)

🛠️ Method: choosing the tense
Step 1 — Is there a finished time expression (yesterday, last, ago, in 2019)? → past simple.
Step 2 — Is there a present-perfect signal (ever, never, already, yet, just, for, since) or a connection to now? → present perfect.
Step 3 — Build the sentence with the matching form.

✏️ Worked paragraph
I have always loved travelling. I have visited several countries, but I have never been to Japan. Last year I went to Turkey with my family, and we spent a wonderful week in Istanbul. I have kept all the photos since that trip. Now I am saving money because I have decided to travel again next summer.

⚠️ Common mistakes
1. Present perfect with a finished time: I have seen him yesterday → I saw him yesterday.
2. Past simple with "since / for" (continuing): She lived here since 2015 → She has lived here since 2015.
3. Wrong participle: I have went → I have gone; I have saw → I have seen.
4. Forgetting have/has: I finished my work already → I have already finished my work.
5. for vs since: for Monday → since Monday; since two years → for two years.

⭐ Recap
- Past simple = finished actions at a definite past time.
- Present perfect = have/has + past participle; links past to present.
- Signals for present perfect: ever, never, already, yet, just, for, since.
- Definite finished time → past simple; unstated or continuing time → present perfect.

📘 Language bank
Past markers: yesterday, last week, two days ago, in 2019, when I was young.
Present perfect markers: ever, never, already, yet, just, for, since, so far, this week.
Irregular participles: gone/been, seen, done, eaten, written, taken, given, made, bought.
Useful sentences: I saw that film last night. / I have never been to Japan. / She has lived here for ten years. / Have you finished your homework yet? / I have just arrived home.

📝 Practice
Exercise 1 — Write the past participle.
go → ______ ; see → ______ ; do → ______ ; eat → ______ ; write → ______ ; be → ______ ; take → ______ ; buy → ______ .

Exercise 2 — Past simple or present perfect? Choose.
1. I (saw / have seen) that film last night.
2. She (never / has never) been to Japan.
3. We (visited / have visited) Rome in 2019.
4. He (has lived / lived) here since 2015.
5. ______ you (finished / ever finished) a marathon?

Exercise 3 — Complete with "for" or "since".
1. I have studied English ______ six years.
2. She has been here ______ Monday.
3. We haven't seen them ______ a long time.
4. They have lived in Tunis ______ 2010.

✅ Answers
Exercise 1: gone/been, seen, done, eaten, written, been, taken, bought.
Exercise 2: 1. saw 2. has never 3. visited 4. has lived 5. Have you ever finished.
Exercise 3: 1. for 2. since 3. for 4. since.

🗣️ Speaking task
Ask a partner about experiences: "Have you ever...?" (travelled abroad, eaten a strange food, met a famous person). If they answer "Yes", ask "When?" and watch how they switch to the past simple to give the time.

👀 Extra note
The key test: is there a finished time expression?
- Yes (yesterday, last week, in 2019, ago) → past simple.
- No, or a link to now (ever, never, already, yet, just, for, since) → present perfect.
And use "for" with a length of time, "since" with a starting point.

📋 Summary
- Past simple: finished action at a definite past time (yesterday, last week, in 2019, ago).
- Form: base + -ed (regular) or irregular past form (went, saw, did); negative didn''t + base; question Did + subject + base.
- Present perfect: have/has + past participle; links a past action to the present moment.
- Regular past participle = base + -ed; irregular participles must be learned (gone/been, seen, done, eaten, written).
- Uses of present perfect: life experiences, actions continuing with for/since, recent actions with a present result, unfinished time periods (today, this week).
- Key signal words: ever, never, already, yet, just, for, since.
- for + a length of time (for three years); since + a starting point (since 2020).
- Golden rule: a definite finished time word forces the past simple, even if "for/since" logic seems tempting elsewhere in the sentence.
- Common trap: "I have seen him yesterday" is wrong — use "I saw him yesterday".

enonce.question:
Read the dialogue.
Maher: Where is Mr Baccar, the sports teacher?
Youssef: I ______ (saw / have seen) him yesterday in the gym.
Maher: And today?
Youssef: No, I ______ (didn't see / haven't seen) him today.

1) Choose the correct form in the first gap. Which word helps you?
2) Choose the correct form in the second gap. Is today finished?
3) Choose: She (visited / has visited) Tozeur last summer.
4) Give two other time expressions that go with the past simple.

Ms Brown, an English teacher, talks to her new Tunisian pupil.
Ms Brown: (you / ever / be) to London?
Hedi: No, I haven't. I have never been to England.
Ms Brown: (you / ever / visit) the Bardo Museum?
Hedi: Yes, I have.
Ms Brown: (your parents / ever / travel) by plane?
Hedi: Yes, they have.

1) Write Ms Brown's three questions in the present perfect.
2) Where do we put ever in the question?
3) Give the past participle of: be, visit, travel.

Two friends talk about a new film at the cinema.
Sami: Is the new adventure film good?
Anas: I don't know. We ______ (not / see) that film yet. My sister ______ (already / buy) the tickets, but my father ______ (not / finish) his work yet.

1) Complete the dialogue with the present perfect.
2) Where do we put yet in the sentence? Is it used here in affirmative or negative sentences?
3) Where do we put already?
4) Write a negative sentence with yet about your homework.
Choose: I ___ (already finished/have already finished) my work.

Read the note on the kitchen table.
Dear Mum, I ______ (go) to the library with Salma. Dad ______ (go) to the market. We ______ (take) the keys. See you at six! — Ines

1) Give the three forms of the verb go: base form, past simple, past participle.
2) Complete the note with the present perfect.
3) Complete the rule: present perfect = have / ______ + past ______.
4) Write the negative of: Dad has gone to the market.

Read about Mr Gharbi.
Mr Gharbi is a teacher of English in Gabès. He started teaching in 2010 and he is still a teacher today. He moved to his present house two years ago.

1) Complete with for or since: ______ two years / ______ 2010 / ______ Monday / ______ a long time.
2) Complete: He has lived in his house ______ two years.
3) Complete: He has taught English ______ 2010.
4) Complete the rule: ______ + a period of time; ______ + a starting point.

Read about Mrs Lamia.
Mrs Lamia came to Mahdia in 2019 and she still lives there today. She started working at the hospital in 2020 and she still works there. She met her best friend, Samia, three years ago, and they are still friends.

1) Complete: She ______ (live) here since 2019.
2) Complete: She ______ (work) at the hospital since 2020.
3) Complete: Lamia and Samia ______ (be) friends for three years.
4) Why do we use the present perfect, and not the past simple, in these sentences?

Read Tarek's message. He makes three mistakes with the past simple and the present perfect.
Hi Bilel! Do you know Mr Smith, our new neighbour? (a) I have seen him last night. (b) He has arrived in Tunis two days ago. (c) I never spoke to an Englishman in my life, so I am a bit shy!

1) Find the time expressions in (a) and (b). Are they finished times?
2) Correct sentences (a) and (b).
3) Correct sentence (c). Which words tell you to use the present perfect?
4) Complete the rule: finished time (last night, ago) → ______; life experience with no exact time → ______.
Explain when to use present perfect.
Which tense with "yesterday, last week, in 2010"?
